newsitem.title: POLAND: GM's Opel to recruit staff for Polish plant.
newsitem.headline: GM's Opel to recruit staff for Polish plant.

text.p: Adam Opel AS, General Motors's German subsidiary, will start recruiting workers for its Polish car assembly plant in March, PAP news agency reported on Wednesday.

Opel will hire about 300 people this year and up to 2,000 by 1998, when the 470 million mark ($275 million) factory in the southern city of Gliwice will be opened, PAP quoted Chritopher Tipon, GM's personnel director in Poland, as saying.
"We will accept applications through local employment offices," PAP quoted Tipon as saying.
Opel plans to assemble 72,000 passenger cars annually from 1998 in the Gliwice plant. It will assemble a low-cost family car based on the Opel/Vauxhall Astra model.
